title: Unveiling Hidden Threats: Using Fractal Triggers to Boost Stealthiness of Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
abstract: arXiv:2511.09252v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Traditional distributed backdoor attacks (DBA) in federated learning improve stealthiness by decomposing global triggers into sub-triggers, which however requires more poisoned data to maintian the attck strength and hence increases the exposure risk. To overcome this defect, This paper proposes a novel method, namely Fractal-Triggerred Distributed Backdoor Attack (FTDBA), which leverages the self-similarity of fractals to enhance the feature strength of sub-triggers and hence significantly reduce the required poisoning volume for the same attack strength. To address the detectability of fractal structures in the frequency and gradient domains, we introduce a dynamic angular perturbation mechanism that adaptively adjusts perturbation intensity across the training phases to balance efficiency and stealthiness. translated_title: 揭示隐藏威胁：利用分形触发器提升联邦学习中分布式后门攻击的隐蔽性
translated_abstract: 传统的联邦学习中的分布式后门攻击（DBA）通过将全局触发器分解为子触发器来提高隐蔽性，然而这需要更多的中毒数据来维持攻击强度，从而增加了暴露风险。为了克服这一缺陷，本文提出了一种新方法，即分形触发的分布式后门攻击（FTDBA），该方法利用分形的自相似性来增强子触发器的特征强度，从而在相同攻击强度下显著减少所需的中毒数据量。为了解决分形结构在频域和梯度域中的可检测性问题，我们引入了一种动态角度扰动机制，该机制在训练的各个阶段自适应地调整扰动强度，以平衡攻击效率与隐蔽性。实验表明，FTDBA仅使用传统方法所需中毒数据量的62.4%即可实现92.3%的攻击成功率。
tldr: 本文提出分形触发的分布式后门攻击（FTDBA），利用分形自相似性增强子触发器特征强度，并通过动态角度扰动机制规避频域和梯度域检测，仅需传统方法62.4%的中毒数据量即达到92.3%的攻击成功率，显著提升了联邦学习后门攻击的隐蔽性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Fractal-Triggered Distributed Backdoor Attack (FTDBA), which leverages fractal self-similarity to enhance sub-trigger feature strength and introduces a dynamic angular perturbation mechanism to evade frequency and gradient domain detection, achieving a 92.3% attack success rate with only 62.4% of the poisoning volume required by traditional methods, significantly boosting the stealthiness of backdoor attacks in federated learning.
